report_name: APT Uses AI and QR Codes in Phishing Attack on Taiwan Researchers

threat_actors.name: Unidentified APT targeting Taiwan
threat_actors.description: An unidentified Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) group conducting a sophisticated spear-phishing campaign against Taiwanese research organizations. The group uses AI-generated lures, QR code phishing, and an adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) framework to bypass MFA. Linguistic analysis of the phishing kit suggests a potential origin in China.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: The primary delivery mechanism is through malicious links in targeted emails sent to Taiwanese research organizations.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing via Service
attack_patterns.description: The attackers used QR codes embedded in legitimate-looking event posters, a form of 'quishing', to direct victims to malicious infrastructure.

attack_patterns.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
attack_patterns.description: An AitM phishing framework was used to intercept credentials and bypass multi-factor authentication by proxying the legitimate Google authentication flow and capturing credentials and MFA tokens in real-time.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack_patterns.description: After a successful Adversary-in-the-Middle attack, the actor hijacks the authenticated session by stealing the victim's session cookie, allowing persistent access to the account.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing via Social Engineering LLM
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor is assessed to have used a large language model (LLM) with a reusable prompt template to generate highly convincing, personalized phishing email lures at scale.

attack_patterns.name: Email Addresses
attack_patterns.description: The attackers gathered email addresses of individuals at specific research organizations in Taiwan to conduct their spear-phishing campaign.

tools.name: AitM Phishing Framework
tools.description: An advanced adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing kit that acts as a reverse proxy to impersonate Google login pages and capture credentials and MFA tokens in real-time using a hybrid HTTP/WebSocket architecture.

tools.name: Large Language Model
tools.description: An AI model suspected to be used by the attackers to generate sophisticated and convincing phishing email content at scale.

identities.name: Taiwanese research organizations
identities.description: A class of organizations in Taiwan targeted by the APT's spear-phishing campaign.

identities.name: Taiwan European Union Centre
identities.description: A reputable institution whose identity was impersonated by the attackers in phishing lures.

identities.name: NCCU Institute of International Relations
identities.description: A reputable institution at National Chengchi University whose identity was impersonated by the attackers in phishing lures.

identities.name: Google
identities.description: The legitimate service whose authentication flow was impersonated by the adversary-in-the-middle phishing framework.

infrastructure.name: AitM Phishing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: A network of phishing sites hosting a convincing replica of a Google login page, acting as a reverse proxy to intercept credentials and MFA tokens.

infrastructure.name: QR Code Phishing Delivery System
infrastructure.description: Physical posters with embedded QR codes used to direct victims' mobile devices to the AitM phishing infrastructure.

indicators.name: Potential Google Brand Impersonation in URL
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Google Brand Impersonation in URL
id: f1a2b3c4-d5e6-4789-a0b1-c2d3e4f5a6b7
status: experimental
description: Detects URLs that contain 'google' in a subdomain but do not belong to a legitimate Google domain. This is a common technique used in phishing attacks to deceive users.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-11985/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-08
tags:
  - attack.t1566.002
  - attack.initial_access
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate third-party services that integrate with Google and use 'google' in their subdomains.
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    cs-host|contains: '.google.'
  filter:
    cs-host|endswith:
      - '.google.com'
      - '.google.org'
      - '.google.net'
      - '.google.dev'
      - '.google.cloud'
      - '.google.co.uk'
      - '.google.ca'
      - '.google.de'
      - '.google.fr'
      - '.google.com.au'
      - '.google.com.tw'
      - '.googleapis.com'
      - '.googlevideo.com'
      - '.google-analytics.com'
      - '.googleadservices.com'
      - '.googlesyndication.com'
      - '.googleusercontent.com'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects URLs that contain 'google' in a subdomain but do not belong to a legitimate Google domain, a common phishing technique.
